Fifth-Confusion Error Debugger

Harmonia chord detector · frozen jazz benchmark · hear the ±P5/±P4 root errors and tell boundary-bleed from a genuine mislabel

93%of ±fifth/fourth root-error TIME is BOUNDARY-BLEED (pooled, duration-weighted)

Of 135s total fifth/fourth root-error, 126s (93%) is the model emitting a neighbor’s root — a fifth/fourth away precisely because V→I and ii→V put neighbors a fifth apart. That is a boundary/timing bleed, not an acoustic mislabel. Only 9s (7%) is a GENUINE fifth-related mislabel of a well-bounded segment.

BOUNDARY-BLEED — predicted root equals the prev or next GT chord’s root, so the model grabbed the fifth-related neighbor (a timing/boundary issue). The matched neighbor is highlighted in the GT-context line.

GENUINE mislabel — predicted root is a fifth away but is not a neighbor’s root, so a well-bounded segment got the wrong fifth-related root (the overtone/acoustic case).

24 clips · each is the error span ±2s of context. Play and listen: for a bleed you should hear the real chord change land inside the clip (the model was just early/late); for a genuine mislabel the whole segment is one chord and simply the wrong root.
